sections.heading: You loved me before I looked for you
sections.text: Father, I would never have gone looking for life and happiness in your love if you had not loved me first. I did not wake myself up. You came after me in grace, and your Spirit made me willing to seek you.
theological_themes: God’s love takes the initiative in salvation.
Human seeking of God is itself a gift of grace.
True happiness is found in being loved by God.

scripture_references.connection: John grounds the believer’s love for God in God’s prior love. This supports the prayer’s confession that seeking and loving God begins with God’s initiative, not human self-generation.
Paul describes salvation as God making the spiritually dead alive because of his mercy and love. That fits the prayer’s acknowledgment that the convert’s turning to God came from grace.

sections.heading: Your Spirit brought me to Jesus
sections.text: Thank you for your Spirit, who helped me see that you have made peace with sinners through Jesus. He taught me to trust that good news, and he helped me receive you as my God, my home, and my greatest treasure.
theological_themes: The Holy Spirit reveals and applies the reconciliation accomplished in Christ.
Faith is a Spirit-enabled response to the gospel.
God himself becomes the believer’s portion and treasure.

scripture_references.connection: Paul teaches that reconciliation is God’s work in Christ, not something sinners create for themselves. This directly grounds the prayer’s trust that peace with God has been made known in Jesus.
Paul says believers receive the Spirit so they may understand what God has freely given them. This supports the prayer’s dependence on the Spirit to recognize and receive the grace of reconciliation.

sections.heading: Thank you for making me your child
sections.text: Blessed forever be your fatherly love. Through faith in Jesus, you have brought me into your family and made me your child. Thank you for giving me even the desire to live like your child—not as a stranger trying to earn a place, but as someone welcomed by you.
theological_themes: Adoption is received through faith in Christ.
God’s fatherly affection gives believers a new identity.
The desire to live as God’s child is itself a gift of grace.

scripture_references.connection: Paul states that believers are children of God through faith in Christ Jesus. This anchors the prayer’s gratitude for being made a child of God by faith in Jesus.
Romans connects adoption, the Spirit’s witness, and the believer’s cry to God as Father. It supports both the confidence of sonship and the Spirit-enabled intimacy expressed in this section.

sections.heading: I need Jesus and the Spirit for every part of this new life
sections.text: In Jesus, my Brother and Savior, I have been given new birth, the power that holds me back from evil, and every grace that renews me. By your Spirit I call you Father, trust you, and love you. Strengthen me deep inside for everything you are calling me to be and do as a Christian.
theological_themes: New birth and renewal come from God, not self-improvement.
Christ supplies the believer’s new life and ongoing help.
The Spirit enables faith, love, obedience, and inner strength.

scripture_references.connection: Paul describes salvation as God’s mercy through regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit, poured out through Jesus Christ. This supports the prayer’s emphasis on new birth and renewing grace coming from Christ by the Spirit.

Paul prays for believers to be strengthened with power through the Spirit in the inner person, with Christ dwelling in their hearts through faith. This closely matches the request for inward strength for the Christian life.

sections.heading: Keep showing me what I have in Christ
sections.text: Please keep opening my eyes to what is truly mine in Christ. Let your Spirit make the riches of your love in him more real to me. Live in me, teach me my union with Jesus, and draw me into steady fellowship with him—not just in rare moments, but as the way I walk with you.
theological_themes: Assurance grows as the Spirit reveals the believer’s share in Christ.
Union with Christ is the basis of fellowship with God.
The Christian life is lived in ongoing dependence on the indwelling Spirit.

scripture_references.connection: Paul says the Spirit bears witness with believers that they are God’s children. This supports the prayer’s request that the Spirit would make the believer’s belonging to Christ known and personally assured.
Jesus teaches that disciples must abide in him and that fruitfulness comes from union with him. This grounds the prayer’s longing for constant fellowship and life in Christ.

sections.heading: Root me deeply in your love
sections.text: Father, teach me to live for you each day and to rejoice in your love. Because I belong to Jesus, let me rest in the love you have for your Son. Root me deeply in that love, like a house built on rock. I know so little. Please grow my understanding and experience of your love in Christ. Keep me pressing forward until I see more and more of its endless fullness.
theological_themes: The Father’s love for believers is received in union with Christ.
God’s love becomes the believer’s stability and foundation.
Growth in the knowledge of God’s love is lifelong and leads toward glory.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus prays that the world would know the Father has loved his people even as he loved the Son, and that the Father’s love would be in them. This supports the prayer’s bold request to rest in the Father’s love through union with Christ.
Paul prays that believers, rooted and grounded in love, would know the immeasurable love of Christ. This directly supports the request for deeper knowledge and experience of divine love.

Jesus describes the wise person as one whose life is built on rock by hearing and doing his words. This illuminates the image of being firmly established in God’s love rather than living on a fragile foundation.

sections.heading: Give according to your love, not my deserving
sections.text: Do not measure your love to me by what I deserve, or even by the weakness of my prayers. Show me your love according to how great it really is. And whatever growth you give me, let it make me love you more in return.
theological_themes: God’s grace is measured by his own love, not human merit.
Prayer depends on God’s generosity rather than the pray-er’s worthiness.
Receiving God’s love should produce greater love for God.

scripture_references.connection: Paul praises God as the one able to do far more abundantly than believers ask or think. This supports the prayer’s request that God would give according to his greatness rather than the smallness of our prayers.
Jesus connects the experience of forgiveness and mercy with great love in response. This supports the prayer’s desire that increased experience of God’s love would draw out deeper love for him.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The line about finding the Father’s love “the same to me as to thy Son” could be misunderstood as erasing the unique eternal sonship of Christ. I rendered it in terms of belonging to Jesus and receiving the Father’s love in union with him, supported by John 17:23-26, while preserving the boldness of the original.
significant_interpretive_choices: I understood “my God and portion” as God being the believer’s home, treasure, and inheritance, rather than merely a religious preference.

I rendered “my interest in Christ” as “what is truly mine in Christ” and “belonging to Christ,” since the older phrase refers to the believer’s personal share in Christ and his benefits, not curiosity about Christ.
I kept the prayer’s strong emphasis on divine initiative: the convert seeks, believes, loves, and grows because the Father has loved first and the Spirit has acted in grace.
